3	You can use Clever Tools to control logs drains, through following commands. Each can target a specific application, adding `--app APP_ID_OR_NAME` or a local alias (`--alias`, `-a`), or a specific add-on, adding `--addon ADDON_ID`:
4

6	clever drain
7	clever drain -F json
8	clever drain create <DRAIN-TYPE> ...
9	clever drain get <DRAIN-ID>
10	clever drain get <DRAIN-ID> --format json
11	clever drain check <DRAIN-ID>
12	clever drain remove <DRAIN-ID>
13	clever drain enable <DRAIN-ID>
14	clever drain disable <DRAIN-ID>
15	```
16	
17	There is one `clever drain create` subcommand per drain type, each exposing only the options it supports:
18	
19	```
20	clever drain create betterstack <DRAIN-URL> --source-token SOURCE_TOKEN
21	clever drain create datadog <DRAIN-URL>
22	clever drain create elasticsearch <DRAIN-URL> --index-prefix INDEX_PREFIX [--username USERNAME] [--password PASSWORD]

Manage drains

I added `clever drain --type <type>`, which lists only the drains of one recipient type. `npm run validate` passes (lint, format, types, docs check, 23 unit tests). I haven't run it against a real account, so the filtering on real drains is untested.

**How it works**
- It takes the same names as `clever drain create <type>`: `betterstack`, `datadog`, `elasticsearch`, `newrelic`, `ovh-tcp`, `raw-http`, `splunk`, `syslog-tcp`, `syslog-udp`.
- The value is checked against that list, so an unknown type fails with: `type: Invalid option: expected one of "betterstack"|"datadog"|…`.
- The CLI still fetches all the drains and filters them itself. The filter applies to both the human and `--format json` output.
- Without `--type`, the command behaves as before. With it and no match, it prints `There are no drains of type <type> for <resource>`.

**Changes**
- `src/commands/drain/drain.options.js`: new `drainTypeOption`, built from the existing list of drain types, so a new drain type is picked up automatically.
- `src/commands/drain/drain.command.js`: the option and the filtering.
- Regenerated `drain.docs.md` and `skills/clever-tools/references/full-documentation.md`.

**Things to know**
- The command docs are regenerated, but the hand-written guide isn't: you didn't approve the edit to `docs/services-logs-drains.md`. It just needs `clever drain --type <DRAIN-TYPE>` added under `clever drain -F json` in the command list at the top. Approve it and I'll add it.
- `node_modules` was missing, so I ran `npm ci` to install the locked dependencies.
- `fix-all` reformatted `.claude/settings.json`, which has nothing to do with this change, so I reverted it.
